analysis.subject: history
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers the secret drafting of a new frame of government, the convention that convened to revise the Articles of Confederation, the wait for a quorum, summer debates, and compromise over power and representation

overview.headline: Secret convention that created a new American government

keyPoints.point: Students learn that delegates drafted the constitution in secret during the summer of 1787.
keyPoints.quote: Drafted in secret by delegates to the Constitutional Convention during the summer of 1787

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the Federal Convention convened in Philadelphia on May 14, 1787 to revise the Articles of Confederation.
keyPoints.quote: The Federal Convention convened in the State House (Independence Hall) in Philadelphia on May 14, 1787, to revise the Articles of Confederation

keyPoints.point: Students learn that members adjourned daily until a quorum of seven states was obtained on May 25.
keyPoints.quote: the members adjourned from day to day until a quorum of seven states was obtained on May 25

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the convention decided to draft an entirely new frame of government rather than amend the Articles.
keyPoints.quote: rather than amend the existing Articles, the Convention would draft an entirely new frame of government

keyPoints.point: Students learn that chief debates concerned power of the central government and representation in Congress.
keyPoints.quote: Among the chief points at issue were how much power to allow the central government

keyTerms.gloss: Meeting of delegates who drafted the constitution in secret during the summer
keyTerms.quote: Drafted in secret by delegates to the Constitutional Convention during the summer of 1787

keyTerms.quote: The Federal Convention convened in the State House (Independence Hall) in Philadelphia on May 14, 1787

keyTerms.quote: the members adjourned from day to day until a quorum of seven states was obtained on May 25

keyTerms.quote: The Federal Convention convened in the State House (Independence Hall) in Philadelphia on May 14, 1787, to revise the Articles of Confederation

keyTerms.quote: Among the chief points at issue were how much power to allow the central government

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Shows students how the convention moved from revision to new drafting in the order taught on the page
componentPlan.focusQuote: All through the summer, in closed sessions, the delegates debated, and redrafted the articles of the new Constitution

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Strengthens recall of key facts about the convention, quorum, and compromise debates
componentPlan.focusQuote: The work of many minds, the Constitution stands as a model of cooperative statesmanship and the art of compromise
